profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 3 campus)
profile.address: 23615 NE Schaaf St, North Hillsboro, OR 97124
profile.reading:
Per Data Center Dynamics' 2020 coverage of QTS's Hillsboro 3 campus opening, this North Hillsboro site, reverse-geocoded to 23615 NE Schaaf St, a separate parcel from the Pubols Street building tracked elsewhere in this registry, is part of the same mega-scale campus first announced in 2018, planned for five data centers totaling 250-plus MW across more than 1 million square feet. Phase 1 opened October 2, 2020 with a 158,000 square foot building and 24 MW of capacity, following a February 2020 groundbreaking on a 27 MW phase. QTS's own current Hillsboro 3 page describes the campus as a planned two-building, 44-acre site with more than 100 MW of total power capacity, built to the company's own QTS Freedom Design standard, and positions the campus as an option for companies seeking Asia-Pacific connectivity or an alternative to Silicon Valley. The same page describes landscaped campus amenities intended to support rapid, large-scale deployments, though it does not itself publish a street address, total square footage, Tier rating, or facility-specific renewable energy figure for this campus.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly ten billion dollar Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release. QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area, Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3, and part of the Portland metro's broader Silicon Forest data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers renewable energy through power purchase agreements. QTS's broader corporate materials describe company-wide practices including closed-loop cooling systems and a stated goal of carbon-free operational electricity, though these are company-level commitments rather than figures confirmed for this specific campus.

Hillsboro's Silicon Forest data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base, anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses, which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses, reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, a pattern similar to the multi-campus expansion seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters.

reading.body:
QTS Hillsboro 3 is a planned five-building megacampus in North Hillsboro, Oregon with 250+ MW total power capacity across more than one million square feet, of which Phase 1 opened in October 2020 with 158,000 sq ft and 24 MW. This specific parcel on Schaaf Street is one of two mapped buildings within the campus, but no per-building power allocation is published by the operator. The campus is part of QTS's three-campus presence in Washington County, a Silicon Forest data center cluster that inherited fiber infrastructure and technical talent from the region's legacy semiconductor manufacturing base.

At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, the campus's 250+ MW total capacity could accommodate roughly 6,250+ racks, though this is an assumption about utilization and load profile, not an operator claim. Oregon ranks ninth among states in published data center capacity with 156.6 MW across eight facilities that disclose figures. The QTS Hillsboro 3 campus, once fully built, would represent the largest single operator commitment in the state by a substantial margin, though no per-phase build schedule or tenant commitments have been published.

QTS is owned by Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust following a roughly $10 billion acquisition completed in August 2021. The campus offers customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements per QTS's own materials. The facility's location in the Portland metro's established data center cluster, combined with its scale and multi-phase development model, positions it to absorb substantial AI compute workloads as the regional grid and operator development timeline permit, though grid constraints for this region are not published.
